summary: SVG illustrations package downloads Bun at preinstall to execute an undeclared 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package presents itself as a static SVG illustrations bundle — package.json `files` allowlists only `illustrations/*.svg` and `CHANGELOG.md`. However, package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, and setup.mjs fetches the Bun runtime from oven-sh's GitHub release archive into a temp directory and then invokes it against `math_init.js`, a ~727KB obfuscated sibling file (obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation with a large numeric array and a rotator function, single-line `_0x`-named symbols). Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are shipped in the tarball but are excluded from the declared `files` allowlist. A static-asset package has no legitimate reason to smuggle an alternate language runtime at install time to run an opaque local blob; the Bun-runs-math_init.js path executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine on `npm install`, and because Bun is invoked instead of Node, the code runs outside the reach of Node-based instrumentation and audit tooling. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern with the payload delivered inside the tarball rather than from a remote host, and the excluded-from-`files` shipping is consistent with a payload added outside the author's declared publish surface.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
